the microstructures of the high-temperature single-phase region (950 °C and 900 °C) were composed of the soft residual br base phase and distributed, hard, and brittle needle-like a'' martensite phase.
Both of these microstructures were remarkably similar, demonstrating dense and fine needle-like a'' martensite phases distributed in the residual b base phase (br).

It can be clearly seen that the 950 °C solid solution-treated alloy had coarser grains than the 900 °C solid solution-treated alloy because a higher temperature resulted in faster crystal grain growth.

we found that the alloys that underwent the solution heat treatment and water quenching at 850 °C and 800 °C both possessed fine needle-like a martensite phases distributed in the b base, as shown in Fig. 2(d) and (e), respectively.

When the solution temperature dropped to 800 °C, the quantity of ap phase in the br base phase was greater than that found in the 850 °C solution-treated sample. These phases were connected in an island shape instead of an isometric shape and showed an elongated shape that was affected by the extruded base material structure. In the comparatively lower-temperature dual-phase region (750 °C), the microstructure of the water-quenched alloy was composed of a residual b base phase and a pro-eutectoid a phase.
With the ''stress-induced martensite phase transformation'' that occurred during the tensile test, the SP-700 Ti alloys experienced a high strength increase and high ductility characteristics.
